paper_metadata.title: Effects of Sb addition on the modification of Mg2Si particles and high-temperature mechanical properties of cast Mg–4Zn–2Si alloy

evidence.quote: The effect of 2 wt.% Si and 0.2 wt.% Sb on the microstructure and high temperature mechanical properties of a cast Mg–4Zn alloy was investigated.

mechanisms.name: particle strengthening by thermally stable intermetallics

evidence.quote: This is due to the presence of high melting point Mg2Si particles with sufficient thermal stability (Tm = 1085 ◦C [6]), which act as high temperature strengthening particles.
the achieved enhancement in mechanical properties can be attributed to both formation of thermally stable Mg3Sb2 particles and to the morphology modification of Mg2Si particles.

This is due to the fact that because of the large stress concentration accumulated on the coarse intersecting branches of Mg2Si particles, cracks can easily nucleate from the interface between these particles and the Mg matrix, reducing the ductility of the Si-containing alloy.

This may be ascribed to the better plasticity of the Mg2Si particles at the investigated test temperature, which can embed the more thermally stable Mg3Sb2 particles (Tm = 1245 ◦C [6]) during large plastic shear deformation.
